events.title: OIC 3018/1978 changes the name of the Ministry of Highways and Public Works to the Ministry of Transportation, Communications and Highways

evidence.locator: OIC 3018/1978, approval stamp 5 December 1978, para (d); recommended 4 December 1978 (chamber date and statutory-authority check)

events.interpretation_notes: The order is approved and ordered 5 December 1978; the 4 December date is the cabinet recommendation, not the change. It names the ministry in the plural ("Communications"); BC Archives' list, from which the episode takes its name, has the singular. An executive naming order: it does not by itself move statutes or staff (OIC 3021/1978 made the transfers of the same day). The same order renames four other ministries, disestablishes Recreation and Conservation and establishes Lands, Parks and Housing, Tourism and Small Business Development, and Deregulation.

events.title: Public Accounts 1898/99 head the Treasury vote "Department of Finance. (Treasury.)", with the Minister of Finance's salary

evidence.locator: Public Accounts for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899 (transmitted Treasury Department, Victoria, 23 December 1899, F. Carter-Cotton, Minister of Finance): printed p. 30, Vote No. 11

events.interpretation_notes: The date is the day the accounts were transmitted, which is when the heading is observed; the vote itself is for 1898/99. It shows the Treasury as the department of the Minister of Finance (in the Executive Council roster, the Minister of Finance and Agriculture). An observation, not the start of the Treasury Department.

match.portfolio: Minister of Transportation, Communications and Highways

add_corroborating_evidence.locator: OIC 3019/1978, approved and ordered 5 December 1978: 'The Honourable Alexander Vaughan Fraser - Minister of Transportation, Communications and Highways'; the order rescinds OICs 3213/76 and 900/78

data_changes.why: The designation order corroborates the Legislative Library roster's start (D3).

code_diffs.why: D2. The 17 unmatched ministry-years are the Treasury Department's 1899-1915. Its alias already maps 'treasury' to the portfolio key 'finance', but until 5 June 1916 the Executive Council styled the portfolio 'Minister of Finance and Agriculture' (key 'finance agriculture'), which matched only the Department of Finance and Agriculture episode. The Public Accounts set the Treasury Department under that minister every year 1899-1916 (18 transmittals, R3H-142 to R3H-164) and head its vote 'Department of Finance and Agriculture. (Treasury.)' in 1903/04 (R3HC-237). Letting an alias name more than one portfolio key fixes it; no term is created, extended or bridged: the 13 Finance and Agriculture terms that overlap 1899-1916 (Carter-Cotton to Campbell) are attached to both episodes on their roster dates. Tested in a copy: 1,069/1,236 terms still matched (no term newly matched or lost), Treasury ministry-years without a minister 17 -> 0, all 2,229 ministry-years covered, node --test 421 pass. Rebuild historyData.js (npm run build:government-history) after applying.

D3, optional. OIC 3018/1978 names the ministry in the plural; BC Archives' list (src/ministries/history.js, kept faithful to its source) has the singular, and SPELLING is where the repository corrects the source's spellings. Consequence: the episode id becomes ministry-of-transportation-communications-and-highways-1978 (from ...-communication-...), so the D3 event's subject_id must be changed with it; nothing else in research/ or src/ refers to the old id (grep; audit/history-import.json is regenerated). Lineage is unchanged (renames pass through spell()); tested in a copy: build and node --test 421 pass. The minister matcher already folds 'communications' to 'communication', so Fraser was matched before and after.
